attackResolution: An attack hits if the player's reported d20 roll + relevant modifiers >= the target's AC. A natural 20 on the die is always a hit and a critical hit (roll damage dice twice); a natural 1 is always a miss. Advantage/disadvantage is reflected by the player rolling twice and reporting which result applies -- take their reported total at face value.
savingThrows: A saving throw succeeds if the player's reported d20 roll + the relevant ability/proficiency modifier meets or beats the DC set for the effect (spell save DC, trap DC, etc.).
skillChecks: A skill or ability check succeeds if the reported roll + modifier meets or beats the DC. Typical DCs: 5 very easy, 10 easy, 15 medium, 20 hard, 25 very hard, 30 nearly impossible.
deathSaves: When a character drops to 0 HP (and isn't killed outright), they are unconscious and must make death saving throws (flat d20, no modifiers) on their turns: 10+ is a success, below 10 is a failure. Three successes stabilizes them at 0 HP; three failures means death. A natural 20 regains 1 HP; a natural 1 counts as two failures. Taking any damage while at 0 HP counts as a failure (two failures if it's a critical hit).
encounterScaling9Players: This party has 9 players, well above the standard 5e assumption of 3-6. When building or narrating encounters, scale enemy count and/or HP pools up significantly and be mindful of action economy -- a 'standard' encounter for 4 players will be trivial here. Prefer more enemies with focused roles over a single heavily-buffed enemy, to keep multiple players engaged each round.
